cards.title: Start stage 0?
cards.text: Shall I make the sample scene in a few looks, a page of voice samples, and the three phone tests?
cards.why: It's 3 to 5 agent-hours and settles the two things a plan can't: whether the look has charm, and whether sound behaves on your iPhone. Nothing else gets built until you've seen them.
cards.pick: Yes. The scene is a hurricane forming over a globe, about 20 seconds, in three or four looks.

cards.title: Pilot lessons
cards.text: You said no lessons in version 1. Can a few small ones drive the build, kept in your private repo?
cards.why: A kit built with no lesson to test it against ends up as parts that look good alone and don't fit together. The app itself would still ship with none.
cards.pick: Three, as unlike as possible: where hurricanes form (globe), what happens when you type a web address (network), ten local birds (cards).
cards.details: If you'd rather other topics, say which. The point is that they use different parts: one map-shaped, one diagram-shaped, one memorising-shaped.

cards.title: A name
cards.text: Primer is only what I called the folder. Which would you keep? Or comment with your own.
cards.why: The repo and the icon on your phone get this name.

options.label: Primer
options.text: A first book on a subject. Also the book in The Diamond Age that teaches one child anything.

options.label: Tinker
options.text: For the playgrounds and taking things apart.

options.label: Whet
options.text: To sharpen, and to whet your curiosity.

options.label: Kiln
options.text: Where things get fired until they hold.

cards.title: The room is your memory
cards.text: Each topic's trophies are the room's furniture, and they dull when that topic's memory fades.
cards.why: It joins your trophies, room and currency into one loop, and pulls you back to review without a streak. Reviewing polishes them. Tap one to review its topic.
cards.pick: Yes. Currency buys the room's bones (walls, floor, lights, shelves); the objects themselves are only earned.
cards.details: The other way is a shop where everything, trophies included, is bought. That's simpler to understand, but then the room says how much you've played, not what you know.

cards.title: A daily streak?
cards.text: Duolingo's hook is the streak. Do you want one?
cards.why: A streak rewards turning up, and losing a long one tends to make people quit. The dulling room does the same job and forgives a week away.
cards.pick: No streak. The room is the pull.

cards.title: A wager in review
cards.text: Before answering, you could tap "sure". Sure and right pays double. Sure and wrong costs you.
cards.why: It makes a wrong answer sting a little, and gives the currency a tie to knowing things. People also fix confidently wrong answers best once they're shown.
cards.pick: Yes, in Review and exams only, and optional each time.

cards.title: Lives in lessons?
cards.text: Should a wrong answer in a lesson cost anything?
cards.why: You want to be able to get things really wrong. If that costs lives, you start playing safe instead of trying things.
cards.pick: No lives in lessons. Exams have a pass mark and a wait before a retake.

cards.title: Playground unlocks
cards.text: How does a part, like the globe, open up for free play?
cards.why: You suggested beating a lesson or paying. Both fit: the tool is something you earned.
cards.pick: Finishing the lesson that introduces it opens it. Currency opens it early. Nothing inside a lesson is locked.

cards.title: Thoroughness
cards.text: Three named levels, or a finer slider?
cards.why: Three is easy to pick from a phone, and each means something clear: Glance is 1 to 2 lessons, Solid 4 to 6 with a test, Deep 10 to 15 or more with an exam.
cards.pick: Three levels. For Solid and Deep, you see and edit the lesson list before anything is built.

cards.title: Where you ask
cards.text: How do you ask for a new topic?
cards.why: Asking from the phone needs a session on the PC waiting for it, like Riffle's. That's worth building once lessons are good, not before.
cards.pick: In chat for stages 1 and 2. From a screen in the app from stage 3, with a place to attach a source.

cards.title: Pictures from the web
cards.text: Which pictures get copied into your lessons?
cards.why: Copied pictures work offline. There's a great deal of openly licensed material (Wikimedia, NASA, open nature photos), so this rarely costs anything.
cards.pick: Open-licensed ones are copied in, with credit. Rights-reserved ones are linked, not copied.

cards.title: Sound on or off
cards.text: Should lessons start with the voice on?
cards.why: Every scene has captions and works by tapping through, so either is fine. This is only where it starts.
cards.pick: Voice on with short captions, a mute button always in reach, and it remembers what you last chose.

cards.title: The take-apart skill
cards.text: Is "teardown" the one you meant: any machine as a 3D model you pull apart and slice?
cards.why: I found no skill called obliterate that does this. If it's a different one, a link or a few more words would find it.
cards.pick: Yes, that one. Build it as a kit part in stage 5: one viewer, each model as data, a question at each build-up step.

cards.title: WorldWise
cards.text: Your geography app from June has a globe, country facts and a passport. What should come across?
cards.why: It's built a different way, so its code doesn't drop in. Its facts and ideas do.
cards.pick: Take its country tables and the globe coloured by how well you know each country. Leave the code and the travel economy.

cards.title: Learning a language
cards.text: When should a language course be tried?
cards.why: It's hundreds of lessons, wants listening and speaking, and lives on the review loop. The app will carry it, but shaping the framework around it now would slow everything else.
cards.pick: As an experiment after stage 3, once Review and the voices are proven. Culture goes in as scenes and real photos.

cards.title: The layout
cards.text: Four tabs along the bottom: Learn, Review, Playground, Room.
cards.why: Learn is a path of lesson nodes for each topic, like Duolingo's. Review is the endless mode. Playground holds the parts you've opened. Room is the cutaway.
cards.pick: These four. A sketch of each screen comes with stage 0's sample scene.

cards.title: Two repos
cards.text: May I make a public repo for the app and a private one for your lessons, as with Riffle?
cards.why: The public one holds only the player and parts, never a lesson, your name or a local path. Your phone will need its own key for the private one, which only you make.
cards.pick: Yes, once the name is settled. Until then the plan is committed on the PC only.
